text: Fomo vs Pump I'm a bit late to the debate but why not have KOL 347th chime in on this highly intellectual discussion. Firstly, it's important to take in the considerations of how trading has moved to retail adoption overall. You have some saying traders are the new NBA players, while I don't think something intellectual can achieve similar status level to athletes or music artists, there is some merit to it. What Ansem said is quite important: "Celebrities, Athletes, Rappers, YouTubers etc are people with high levels of influence and usually money. Since they command so much attention and respect, they can monopolize their followings, except they can't teach their followers their success. Robert Downey Jr can't explain to a normal person how to be a star actor. Lebron can't teach someone how to hoop. Drake can't teach someone how to top the leaderboards for a decade straight. However traders can. They can give you their thought processes, risk management, catalysts, second/third order effects, a look inside their mind etc." This is the magic. Traders are uniquely positioned to build an audience which can benefit if they're: 1) successful 2) good at communicating their ideas They have the ability to teach others and grow their reputation unlike any other celebrity or person of influence online. The rise of TJR style characters is confirmation of this. His type definitely aren't what we need, although those with genuine research and teams around them like Ansem and Threadguy are doing some important pioneering whether you like them or not. The question arises "why hasn't this happened before if trading has been around for so long?". The answer is due to trading being mostly a walled garden. Many doors have opened over the past decade for the average person to be exposed to nearly every type of asset class. This is only accelerating. Your average joe is looking for a way out. Paychecks are providing less of a comfort barrier to everyday life which has caused the influx of retail trading. Especially now that the average person can close the gap with AI tooling if they're willing to put in the work. Social trading offers more accessibility, more transparency, more viral PNLs for retail to get sucked in by. A friend said something along the lines of "imagine if we had Fomo in the 24' meme era". Imagine the amount of 24hr 7-8 fig PNLs there would have been. At this stage everyone knows green candle therapy is the best way to get returning customers to our business. I've noticed people discussing new floors more frequently over the past month. Everyone's coming to realization how crazy the runners were from the 24/25 era. Coins would go mid 9 figs on a random Tuesday and nobody blinked an eye. While it's hard to tell if we've had a genuine onboarding of new participants through the TikTok/social trading wave as most of the numbers on Fomo are obviously spoofed to bring higher valuations, this will be the key catalysts for entering another onchain bull. The higher Fomo keeps their fees and continuous swap failures, more will transition to Pump along with the fat cash bonuses. Pump doesn't need to innovate more, their war chest lets them play the game of stalking a strong pivot once a new comer shows innovation and trend setting. For active traders and more importantly those who communicate on socials well, this war is a goldmine as you essentially become a prize fighter for whichever platform wants you on their leaderboard. Even though Fomo have explicitly said they're going the IPO route, I don't think this is true. Why would they spend significantly more time and risk losing their lead to become "the home of trading" or some "institutional onboarding app". It seems smart from their end to keep raking in their mid 6 fig daily revenue and continue to onboard as much volume as possible until Pump or others catch up. Once they see an opportunity for the bull to come back or mass onboarding of new users due to an unforeseen catalyst, then launch a native token.

text: If a team was going to go a IPO route, Hyperliquid would have been the best liquid play thus far but even they know the power of a strong flywheel and tokenomics. Intentions aren't on the table here, every founders goal is to cash out and maximise as much profit as possible. Yes, maybe Fomo's playing the long game, a native token still would make more sense if they're serious operators. I've always bashed on people who take payouts, partnerships, affiliates etc, as most are doing it purely for the money and they have no ties to their actual brand. Social trading apps on the other hand are one of the only exceptions I see to this. We're all traders, more credit to those who post about their trades publicly and then back it up on a public wallet. They're easy to bash on because it's right in front of your face, but to do it successfully is an entirely different feat and deserves its flowers. We've progressively seen less and less airdrops overtime as the speculative ball of money has been fragmented like a school of fish during a feeding frenzy. If Pump, Fomo or any other trading app drop a fat pay check on your lap for doing the thing you've already been doing, you'd be dumb not to take it at this stage of the bear market. While social trading apps feel like they have an evil presence about them, I think it's a step forward in our industry, especially as we operate on so much insider info despite blockchains "transparency". The 8/9 figure CT chads are nowhere to be seen, as leaderboards become more adopted, the proof will be in the pudding for who's genuinely larping.
